activation: Only after A verification and B fixture/integration gates; no C1 before both pass.
scannerApi: export function scan({ path, source, policy, modules, catalog }) returning Finding[] synchronously; export const extensions = array of handled extensions including leading dot

finding.syntax: nonempty canonical offending syntax without position/trivia; AST printer or parsed declaration normalization, not whole file

fingerprint: Orchestrator SHA256 of JSON.stringify([ruleId,path,syntax]); count occurrences per fingerprint. Position never participates. Counts may decrease; no new fingerprint or increased count accepted in audit mode.

policy.tokenCssNames: array of all registered CSS token names
policy.resolvedTokens: id to resolved value map; canonical generated tokens are read-only
policy.note: Scanners report raw findings. Registry exceptions and baseline ledger accounting applied centrally; never silently exempt broad directories in scanners.
policy.resolvedCssTokens: Optional for fixture compatibility; canonical policy.mjs always supplies exact declared CSS custom property to resolved value map. When supplied, it must cover every tokenCssNames entry exactly. Do not derive CSS names from token IDs.
policy.loader: scripts/design-system-locks/policy.mjs validates both canonical token sources using the Stage A graph validator and creates deterministic tokenCssNames, resolvedTokens and resolvedCssTokens.
policy.required: Audit requires an explicitly supplied live policy. Missing/null policy is fatal. An explicit empty registered-token policy is permitted for intentional isolated fixtures; production policy is loaded from validated canonical token sources.
policy.identity: tokenCssNames contains unique valid CSS custom-property names. If resolvedCssTokens is supplied, its key set must exactly equal that unique token set.

failClosed: Parser failures and unsupported governed syntax must become explicit findings or errors, never empty success. Orchestrator treats scanner exceptions as blocking; no baseline for infrastructure/parser errors.
baseline: Every existing-debt fingerprint references an owned temporary ledger entry with replacement, expiryCheckpoint and exact rule/path/fingerprint boundary. No total-count-only baseline; no auto-rebaseline command in CI.
exceptions: Permanent exceptions registered with exact path/rule boundary and reason; temporary entries expire by ordered checkpoints A,B,C1,C2,C3,C4,C5,C6. Reject missing owners/replacements/expiry, duplicate/unknown entries and expired entries.
currentCheckpointGovernance: Single source of truth for which checkpoint the audit enforces. scripts/design-system-locks/current-checkpoint.mjs reads exactly this field (never a literal in package.json, CI YAML, or any other file) and audit.mjs's isExpired() compares every ledger entry's expiryCheckpoint against it. Checkpoints are an ordered stage sequence (design-system-migration-plan.md), not calendar dates: 'not a date any batch is due' (stage-b-closure-summary.md). Advancing this value is the lead's decision (see ownership) and requires the closing checkpoint's own exit criteria to be met first (e.g. C1's: docs/internal/design/evidence/c1-execution-record.md '## Batch close') — a reviewed, versioned edit here, never a silent default. Moving this value forward past a checkpoint that still has owned ledger entries at or before it is exactly what is supposed to make the audit fail on that debt (expired-ledger); that is not a regression to work around by re-dating the entries.
sourceScope: Complete applicable src tree plus packages/ui/src when present, including CSS/JS/JSX/TS/TSX/SVG. Canonical src remains required. Tests, stories, generated token definitions and third-party/adaptor boundaries must be enumerated centrally as reviewed boundaries, not implicit scanner skip logic. Governed extension matching is case-insensitive.

ownership.policy.mjs: lead: canonical policy loading and integration
ownership.current-checkpoint.mjs: lead: reads currentCheckpoint above; the only legal source of the --checkpoint value any caller passes to audit.mjs

integrationFreeze: Workers modify only new scripts/design-system-locks, tests/design-system-locks and assigned enforcement files. No existing Stage A files, package/lock/config/CI, application files, or generated outputs. Lead integrates after A gate.
coverageApi: coverage.mjs exports checkCoverage({root,indexPath,evidencePaths}) returning {errors: string[]}; compose existing Stage A validators read-only, no scanner API required.
moduleContext: Audit supplies modules as a frozen plain object mapping every collected governed POSIX path to its source string, rooted in that audit invocation. Current source equals modules[path]. Isolated scanner calls may omit context, but unresolved imports then remain unsupported. Scanners must not read another checkout through process.cwd or unscoped filesystem access; missing modules, cycles, and unsupported callees cannot be assumed safe.
sourceFilesystem: Source roots and entries must be physical regular directories/files. Symbolic links are rejected with structured source-filesystem errors; external targets are never followed. Directory/stat/read failures produce blocking report evidence, never silent empty success.
catalogContext: Audit supplies a separately deep-frozen catalog snapshot from the requested root design-system/catalog.json when controls.mjs is loaded. The object has version and entries with source, exports, publicExports and publicTypes arrays; relevant shapes are validated. Missing/malformed required catalog is fatal invalid-catalog. Injected non-controls fixtures may omit it; controls requires explicit valid context when classifying UI imports. No scanner-owned filesystem read or global cross-root classification cache.
runtimeBoundaryClassification: A scanner may classify a proven direct runtime paint parameter/member read at a known DOM style, SVG or canvas paint site as a blocking extension-boundary, identified by exact path/rule plus stable receiving symbol, receiver kind, paint property and AST-normalized expression. This is not an exemption and does not assert contrast compliance. Static definitions/defaults/fallbacks remain independently scanned. Opaque calls, store/variant outputs, unknown receivers and unproven transforms remain unsupported. Exact central ledger/registry approval is required; status chrome remains governed and temporary migration obligations expire at the assigned checkpoint.
safeAreaPolicy: A syntactically valid env() for exactly safe-area-inset-top/right/bottom/left without its required fallback is a specific spacing/missing-safe-area-fallback policy violation, not an unsupported parser case. It stays blocking for new debt and may enter an exact owned temporary C1 ledger whose replacement supplies a justified closed-scale fallback. Malformed syntax, unknown names and unproven expressions remain parse/unsupported failures. A valid closed-scale fallback remains a centrally reviewed runtime extension boundary; invalid static fallback stays off-scale. No env() wildcard exemption is permitted.
arbitraryTextTypePolicy: A well-formed text-[var(--...)] utility without a color:/length: hint whose kind cannot be proven from the canonical token policy emits blocking typography/missing-arbitrary-type-hint debt. Its exact owned C1 replacement states the intended type and separately resolves any undefined token. A type hint never approves an unknown token. Malformed, interpolated or otherwise unhandled grammar remains unsupported; statically proven registered kinds retain their existing checks.
unverifiedGovernedValuePolicy: ts-colors/unverified-governed-value is permitted only when parsing succeeded and an exact governed styling sink is proven with stable receiving identity and AST-normalized expression, but the direct value is not statically token-proven. Missing/cyclic modules, opaque helper/variant/store provenance, unknown receiver/property, computed properties and whole style objects remain unsupported. Static definitions and raw fallbacks remain independently scanned. This rule is blocking debt requiring exact owned temporary ledger review; it is never an automatic exemption or a generic replacement for unsupported findings.
